title: This Lenovo Deal Makes a Strong Case for Upgrading Your Laptop
gist: Wired's deal piece says Lenovo's IdeaPad Slim 5x (Snapdragon X2 Plus, 16GB, 512GB OLED) is down $250 to $900, in a market where an ongoing memory shortage has pushed laptop prices up, including Apple's. A lower-resolution version sells for $800 at Lenovo.com.

insights.claim: The industry is suffering from an ongoing memory shortage without signs of slowing down.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: DRAM supply tightness is a pricing tailwind for memory makers and headwind for PC OEM margins.
insights.quote: an industry suffering from an ongoing memory shortage

insights.claim: Increasing memory prices have forced laptop manufacturers, including Apple, to raise prices across the board; excellent $900 laptops were common a year ago but are not now.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Component cost inflation passes through to consumers.
insights.quote: Increasing memory prices have forced laptop manufacturers to raise their own prices across the board

insights.claim: The high-end IdeaPad Slim 5x (16GB, 512GB, 2560x1600 OLED, Snapdragon X2 Plus) is $900 on Amazon, $250 off and its lowest price; the 1920x1200 version is $800 at Lenovo.com, 18% off.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Discounting by Lenovo despite cost pressure signals inventory or competitive dynamics.

insights.claim: Qualcomm's Snapdragon X2 Plus is in the same league as Apple's M5 in CPU performance but rarely appears in affordable laptops this year; graphics are not suited to video editing, 3D or serious gaming.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Windows-on-Arm silicon is reaching CPU parity with Apple's but lags in graphics.

insights.claim: The Dell XPS 13 also sells for $900, but is a small portability-focused device versus the IdeaPad's 15.3-inch screen at 0.61 inches thick.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Competitive positioning in the sub-$1,000 premium segment.
